items.markdown:
You can prevent or slow down certain types of hair loss by `managing underlying health conditions, using targeted medications, and protecting your hair from physical damage`.[[1]](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21753-hair-loss)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JwL1yS5Su5U&t=8)

### Medical and Over-the-Counter Treatments

- **Minoxidil:** Available over-the-counter as a liquid, foam, or shampoo ([Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/hair-loss/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20372932) ) to help regrow hair or slow down thinning.[[1]](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/hair-loss/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20372932)
- **Finasteride:** A prescription pill for men (Mayo Clinic ) that lowers dihydrotestosterone (DHT) levels to slow hair loss and promote new growth.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1imyJKMWy2U&t=26)[[2]](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/hair-loss/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20372932)
- **Other Medications:** Options like spironolactone or oral dutasteride may be prescribed by a doctor for specific hormonal or pattern hair loss ([Cleveland Clinic](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21753-hair-loss)).[[1]](https://www.health.harvard.edu/skin-and-hair-health/its-not-too-late-to-save-thinning-hair)[[2]](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/hair-loss/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20372932)
- **Dermatologist Evaluation:** Consult a board-certified dermatologist ([American Academy of Dermatology](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/hair-loss/treatment/tips) ) to diagnose the exact cause of your hair loss before starting a treatment plan.[[1]](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/hair-loss/treatment/tips)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IaAmwIl2l9I&t=215)

### Lifestyle and Diet Habits

- **Eat a Balanced Diet:** Consume enough protein, iron, zinc, and vitamins (like B-vitamins and vitamin D) ([Hers](https://www.forhers.com/guides/how-to-prevent-hair-loss-in-women) ) to support healthy hair follicles. Avoid crash dieting or severe calorie restriction (American Academy of Dermatology).[[1]](https://www.forhers.com/guides/how-to-prevent-hair-loss-in-women)[[2]](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21753-hair-loss)[[3]](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/hair-loss/treatment/tips)
- **Manage Stress:** High stress can trigger temporary shedding (telogen effluvium) (Hers ); use exercise, meditation, or relaxation techniques to cope.[[1]](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21753-hair-loss)[[2]](https://www.forhers.com/guides/how-to-prevent-hair-loss-in-women)
- **Treat Medical Conditions:** Properly manage thyroid disease, autoimmune issues, or other underlying health problems (Cleveland Clinic).[[1]](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21753-hair-loss)

### Hair Care and Styling Protection

- **Avoid Tight Hairstyles:** Stop wearing tight buns, ponytails, braids, or cornrows that pull on the scalp (American Academy of Dermatology).
- **Limit Chemical and Heat Damage:** Cut back on bleaching, perming, chemical relaxing, hot-oil treatments, curling irons, and flat irons (American Academy of Dermatology ). Use blow-dryers on the lowest heat setting.
- **Wash and Detangle Gently:** Use a mild shampoo ([Healthline](https://www.healthline.com/health/hair-loss-prevention) ) suited to your scalp and a wide-tooth comb to detangle wet hair without snapping the shafts.
- **Quit Smoking:** Smoking can contribute to oxidative stress (Healthline ) and damage hair follicles.[[1]](https://www.healthline.com/health/hair-loss-prevention)[[2]](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21753-hair-loss)[[3]](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/hair-loss/treatment/tips)[[4]](https://store.mayoclinic.com/education/hair-thinning-vs-hair-shedding-products/)

If you'd like to narrow this down, tell me:

- Are you noticing **gradual thinning** (like a receding hairline or widening part) or **sudden shedding**?
- Are you looking for options for a **man** or a **woman**?
